speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like classic angina; have you noticed any changes in your risk factors, such as high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or a family history of heart disease? Also, do you smoke or consume alcohol regularly?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I've been dealing with high blood pressure and high cholesterol for about ten years. I also smoke heavily, having accumulated 20 pack-years, though I only drink socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: That combination of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and heavy smoking significantly increases your risk for coronary artery disease. Have you experienced any chest pain while at rest, or has the frequency of these episodes increased recently? REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG) REQUEST TEST: Lipid_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrocardiogram: ST segment depression in leads I, AVL, V4-V6 suggestive of ischemia. Lipid Panel: Total Cholesterol 250 mg/dL (elevated), LDL 160 mg/dL (elevated), HDL 40 mg/dL, Triglycerides 180 mg/dL.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ECG confirms ischemia, and your lipid panel shows significant dyslipidemia. Have you ever experienced a sudden, severe "tearing" pain in your chest or back, or any symptoms of heart failure like waking up at night gasping for air? REQUEST TEST: Troponin_I REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the normal troponin and echocardiogram help rule out an acute heart attack and structural heart failure. Given your classic exertional symptoms and confirmed ischemia, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles, or do you feel unusually tired and weak during daily activities?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't noticed any swelling in my legs or ankles, and while I get winded during my episodes, I don't feel generally weak or unusually tired during my normal daily tasks.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your symptoms are strictly exertional and resolve with rest, and we have ruled out acute infarction and heart failure, have you noticed any pain radiating to your jaw, neck, or left arm during these episodes? Additionally, do you experience any indigestion, heartburn, or a sour taste in your mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, the tight squeezing pain definitely shoots down into my jaw and left arm during the episodes. I do not experience any indigestion, heartburn, or a sour taste in my mouth.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the classic exertional nature of your pain, the radiation to your jaw and arm, and the confirmed ischemia on your ECG, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Stable Angina Pectoris secondary to Coronary Artery Disease.
